reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited paragraphs support it: p0083 gives an unqualified Vendor defend/indemnify obligation for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, extended to Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel.

p0084 supplies the remaining preferred limbs (Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorised access to/disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus fraud and bodily injury/property damage), so the rule's model language is met or exceeded.

p0086 contains the standard procedure (prompt notice with material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, no prejudicial settlement without consent), and p0087 adds procure/modify/replace/refund remedies expressly in addition to the defence obligation.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in p0085 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised; Customer's violation of Applicable Law), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination and Vendor instructions — consistent with the preferred position that Customer's indemnity stays narrow.

No redline or counterparty comment is expected or present for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is unchanged from the original paragraphs and the deterministic check confirms a Vendor IP indemnity is present. Rationale's supporting note on Excluded Claims (p0091) is accurate.
